result.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
result.summary: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B executor, the selected harnesses lead the reported Qwen3-4B comparisons, achieving 95.41% on ALFWorld, 70.56% on DBBench, 48.17% on WebShop, and 41.67% on OSBench. Across three improvers and three edit scopes, from skill text to single-component and coordinated executable edits, GPT-6.1 Sol shows the largest average gain from the broadest scope. Our code is available at https://huangshengzebluesky.github.io/hookevo/.

AI.brief_summary: HookEvo 利用 agent runtime 的生命周期 hook，让独立改进器从执行轨迹诊断失败、联合编辑可执行插件及任务内共享状态，并在匹配任务上与当前 harness 对比择优、逐轮迭代，冻结 Qwen3-4B 后在 ALFWorld 等四个基准报告结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「tool receipt 可写入共享状态并控制后续上下文与动作」的插件机制，可供核查作为视觉证据进入推理状态并驱动 LOOK/STOP 的架构线索；但纯文本设定与 latent 表示、视觉细节保留的联系尚不明确。
